clue.text: Often a confidant got a step wrong

indicators.note: done wrong, these letters are put together in a different order

explanation.surface: Someone you trust with secrets has made a misstep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges GOTASTEP. The definition plays on the saying 'between you, me and the gatepost', where the post is the silent sharer of a secret.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'between you, me and the gatepost' makes the post a figurative keeper of secrets.

clue.text: Going after second hundred from the start, score heavily

indicators.note: from the start of each word means its first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A scorer piling on runs after reaching a second century from the beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the start' takes the first letters of the four words.
explanation.definitionFit: To gash is to cut deeply, to score heavily in the sense of marking with a deep cut.

clue.text: Hand over avenger, so ordered to react, although late

parts.note: to turn in is to hand over, as to the police

indicators.note: ordered means arranged in a fresh order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An avenger is told to give himself up, then reacts belatedly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' rearranges AVENGERSO into ONESGRAVE. 'late' means dead: a dead person reacting is said to turn in their grave.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone long dead is said to turn in their grave when something would have upset them in life.

clue.text: Drops the broken fragment

indicators.note: broken means smashed apart, so the letters are reassembled differently

explanation.surface: Someone drops the shattered piece of pottery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges DROPSTHE.
explanation.definitionFit: A potsherd is a broken piece of pottery, a fragment found by archaeologists.

clue.text: Show sorrow over end of repentant monstrosity

parts.note: to sigh is to show sorrow

indicators.note: the end of the word means its last letter is taken

explanation.surface: Grieving over the outcome of a penitent's terrible deed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of' takes T from 'repentant'; 'over' is a link (in a down clue it means placed above).
explanation.definitionFit: A sight, informally, is something ugly or ridiculous to look at, an eyesore.

clue.text: Dim-witted baronet drowned in river

indicators.note: something drowned in a river lies within it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the Ouse is a river in Yorkshire (and another in Sussex)

explanation.surface: A slow-witted aristocrat has drowned in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drowned in' signals the container; the Ouse is a river in Yorkshire, and 'Dim' tempts towards a word about light.
explanation.definitionFit: Obtuse means slow to understand, a synonym of dim-witted.

clue.text: Bear a resemblance, perhaps

definitions.meaning: to be similar, read as two words
an archaic word for probably or perhaps

explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it means be similar; as one archaic word it means probably.

clue.text: Depressed and hurt, we need heart treatment

indicators.note: giving the words treatment works them over into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A gloomy, injured patient says we need cardiac care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treatment' rearranges HURTWENEEDHEART; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling under the weather means slightly unwell or low in spirits.

clue.text: From east to west, extremely hot before it's all over

parts.note: very means extremely
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: Across the whole country, it's scorching right up to the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From' and 'to' are links giving the order E ... W, and 'it's' is a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Everywhere means in every place, all over.

clue.text: Spoilt brat made known publicly

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child
aired means broadcast, made public

explanation.surface: A pampered child's misdeeds were broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoilt' looks like part of 'spoilt brat' but means damaged.
explanation.definitionFit: Impaired means damaged or weakened, spoilt in that sense.

clue.text: Reject excellent pastries? It's a trick

indicators.note: to reject is to throw back, so the whole run of letters is turned round

parts.note: mega is slang for excellent
tarts are pastries

explanation.surface: Refusing some superb pastries turns out to be a ruse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reject' turns MEGATARTS round as a whole. 'It's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A stratagem is a scheme or ruse, a trick meant to outwit someone.

clue.text: Beaver found here, having died in a box

indicators.note: the letter for died is placed in the word for a box

parts.note: a loge is a box in a theatre
d is the abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: An animal discovered dead in a crate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts D inside LOGE, a theatre box. A beaver's home is its lodge.
explanation.definitionFit: A beaver's dwelling of sticks and mud is called its lodge.

clue.text: Ruin the food that's been prepared

definitions.meaning: to ... someone's chances is to wreck them

explanation.definitionFit: Dish as a verb means spoil or wreck; as a noun it is a cooked item served at a meal.

clue.text: Author of Cutter in the Silv'ry River

indicators.note: one piece is set in the river, so it is placed inside the river's name

parts.note: the Tay, celebrated in McGonagall's poem 'The Silvery Tay', a Scottish river
a hacker is one who cuts or chops

explanation.surface: Looks like the title of a book by some writer, set on a shining river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the container. William McGonagall's notoriously bad poem praises the Scottish 'silvery' Tay; the italics make the clue look like a book title, and 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: William Makepeace Thackeray was a Victorian novelist, author of Vanity Fair.

clue.text: Lily needs a little space with a name like this

parts.note: a gap is a small space
thus means in this way

explanation.surface: A lily needs some room and a suitably fancy name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs' and 'with' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Agapanthus is the African lily, a garden plant with blue flower heads.

clue.text: Sellers perhaps with history make a formal statement

parts.note: Peter Sellers was one of the Goons of the BBC radio comedy The Goon Show
a record is a history, an account of past events

explanation.surface: Salespeople with a track record issue an official declaration.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter Sellers, the comic actor, was a member of The Goon Show cast, a classic British radio comedy; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To go on record is to state something publicly and officially.

clue.text: Put bowl in fridge — one left out is silly

indicators.note: out means taken away, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: to chill a dish is to put a bowl in the fridge
a single L, standard for left

explanation.surface: Putting a bowl in the fridge and leaving one out is daft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes one L from CHILLDISH. 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Childish means immature, so foolish or silly.

clue.text: This is no secret — not keeping quiet at all, it gets around

indicators.note: something that gets around goes round in a circle, so letters move from one end to the other
not keeping something means letting it go, so those letters are taken out

parts.note: hush-hush means secret

indicators.note: at all here means every instance, so the word for quiet is removed both times it appears

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet

explanation.surface: A rumour spreads because no one could keep quiet about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not keeping' with 'at all' removes both SHs from HUSHHUSH, leaving HUHU; 'it gets around' moves the front H to the end. 'This is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Uh-uh is an informal spoken negative, meaning no.

clue.text: Everybody present is of normal intelligence

definitions.meaning: the whole group has turned up

explanation.definitionFit: All there means everyone is present; of a person it means mentally alert and sane.

clue.text: Look closely, and count, perhaps

definitions.meaning: a count is a nobleman, one example of a member of the peerage

explanation.definitionFit: Peer means look hard at something; it is also a noble, of which a count is one kind.

clue.text: Snake following cow finds anemone

parts.note: to snake is to wind, as a path does
f is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
a cow lows, so it is a lower

explanation.surface: A snake trailing behind a cow comes upon a flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cow' as LOWER means 'one that lows' (moos), not 'lower' meaning further down. 'finds' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Windflower is an old name for the anemone, from Greek anemos, wind.

clue.text: Geographical feature — topic anyone covers

indicators.note: the words cover the answer, holding it inside them

explanation.surface: A topic everyone covers in geography class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covers' points to the letters inside 'topic anyone'.
explanation.definitionFit: A canyon is a deep gorge, a landform studied in geography.

clue.text: Mean yokel heartlessly and endlessly drawing back

indicators.note: drawing back means pulling in reverse, so the whole assembly is read from right to left
without its heart, the word keeps only its outside letters
with no end, the last letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: dragging is drawing, as in pulling something along

explanation.surface: A stingy country bumpkin cruelly and constantly recoils.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartlessly' strips the middle of 'yokel', 'endlessly' trims the last letter, and 'back' turns the whole assembly round. 'Mean' is the stingy sense, not 'signify'.
explanation.definitionFit: Niggardly means stingy or miserly, which is mean in the British sense.

clue.text: Long time before noon

parts.note: a year is a period of time

explanation.surface: Ages pass before midday arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' is a link; 'Long' is the verb, as in long for.
explanation.definitionFit: To yearn is to long for something, a synonymous verb.

clue.text: Drop when row is heard

indicators.note: something heard is spoken, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats

explanation.surface: A fall happening just as an argument can be overheard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' rhymes with 'cow' here in the surface (a quarrel) but means a line, TIER. 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A tear is a drop of liquid from the eye, a teardrop.

clue.text: Light rain ends up nearly a foot deep

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: tips are ends

explanation.surface: Drizzle collects until it is almost a foot deep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses TIPS. 'nearly a foot deep' is a second definition: a spit is the depth of a spade's blade, about a foot.
explanation.definitionFit: Spitting is the lightest kind of rain, a few scattered drops.

clue.text: Old house beside a track

parts.note: ry, for railway, a track

explanation.surface: An ancient home standing next to a path.
explanation.walkthrough: RY (railway) for 'track' is a crossword convention; 'beside' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoary means grey with age, so very old.

clue.text: Chips and peas amalgamated in a capsule …

indicators.note: amalgamated means blended together, so the letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A recipe line: chips and peas mixed into a little container.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amalgamated' rearranges CHIPSPEAS; 'and' and 'in' are links. The ellipsis carries on to the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A space capsule is a small spacecraft, so a spaceship.

clue.text: … going out with 4

definitions.meaning: dating someone, being in a relationship with them
clue 4's answer, the faculty of vision

explanation.definitionFit: To be seeing someone is to date them; seeing is also the power of vision, sight.

clue.text: Fly perhaps after receiving note behind closed doors

indicators.note: the insect receives the note, so the note goes inside it

parts.note: a fly is an example of an insect
re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A fly, having taken in a note, retreats into privacy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after receiving' signals the container: the fly, as an example of its class, takes the note inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Done behind closed doors means done privately, out of public view.
